Rasmussen's Encephalitis: The patient's presentation of recurrent seizures, progressively more frequent seizures despite antiepileptic therapy, hemiparesis with brisk reflexes, focal abnormal brain activity concordant with seizure semiology, and cognitive decline are consistent with Rasmussen's Encephalitis. The presence of unihemispheric atrophy on imaging also supports this diagnosis.
Hemispheric Stroke: The patient's history of recurrent seizures, left-sided weakness, marked asymmetry of the cerebral hemispheres, significant atrophy of the right cerebral hemisphere, and hemiparesis are consistent with Hemispheric Stroke. The upper motor neuron pattern on examination and cortical atrophy on imaging also support this diagnosis.
